source.title: Towards practical quantum neural network diagnostics with neural tangent kernels
source.authors: Francesco Scala; Christa Zoufal; Dario Gerace; F. Tacchino

record.tranche_reason: The study sweeps QNN parameter counts and reports test-set inference metrics for QNTK-based predictions. This is a conceptual test of model-size effects on generalization, but it does not use the original double-descent method or directly measure the full claimed curve.
record.gate_note: The paper reports test R² or test accuracy versus parameter count in Figs. 2, 9, and 12. These are QNTK-based inference diagnostics, not direct measurements of test error for trained QNNs. The text does not report numerical values or describe a fall-rise-fall curve. Training MSE and epoch counts versus parameter count are not rows for the claim's test-error versions. No epoch-wise test-error sweep or sample-size sweep is reported.
record.test_reason: The paper is about using the quantum NTK at initialization to diagnose QNN training speed, critical learning rate and approximate inference. It never examines double descent, an interpolation-threshold peak, or test error against model size as a phenomenon. Its only link to the topic is citation [55] (Adlam & Pennington, triple descent) inside a list of NTK references. The test-metric curves (Figs. 2d, 9d, 12d) score the QNTK kernel formula (Eq. 9), which fits all training points exactly by construction. They are not trained-QNN test error across an interpolation threshold, so they cannot show a fall-rise-fall shape. The text describes no peak.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is correct. The authors conclude that the initialization QNTK spectrum gives a critical learning rate (2/λmax) and a training decay time (2κ), and that a QNTK kernel formula approximates inference. The approximation is accurate for deep, near-lazy QNNs and still informative for shallow ones. They draw no conclusion about double descent.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses QNTK spectra and kernel-based inference diagnostics, rather than measuring double-descent curves as in the cited original sources.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported inference diagnostics vary with dataset, encoding frequency, ansatz, and parameter count; agreement with trained-QNN predictions also depends on depth and parameter change during training.

fits_no_version.finding: QNTK kernel-inference predictions (Eq. 9) of test R² or accuracy, plotted against parameter count for four QNN designs on three datasets. High-frequency encodings are diagnosed as increasingly prone to overfitting as depth grows, while low-frequency ones generalize better. Figure values are not given in the text.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For quantum neural networks, the initialization-stage QNTK kernel predictor indicates test performance that depends on encoding frequency, with high-frequency encodings overfitting as parameters grow.

record.problems: The reported test curves are QNTK-based diagnostics rather than direct test-error measurements of trained QNNs. The relevant curves are shown in figures without numerical values or a textual account of their full shapes; results are averaged over 10 initializations.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant test metrics were reported outside the plotted QNTK test R² or accuracy curves in Figs. 2d, 9d, and 12d.

untested.parts: All: no trained-model test error versus size around an interpolation threshold.

record.verdict_notes: Relation is set to cites_only because the only connection is a citation to an NTK triple-descent paper [55] within a reference list. The reader's 'tests/T2' should be dropped. All rows are QNTK-predictor diagnostics with figure-only values; they should be relinked to none or removed.

versions.untested_parts: The paper reports QNTK-based test metrics across parameter counts, but does not directly report trained-QNN test error or establish a fall-rise-fall curve with a peak near the interpolation threshold.
